findings.title: Cutover script's "report is always written" guarantee does not hold for unchecked exceptions
`strip_new_args` hardcodes the replication host, duplicating the cluster table
findings.description: `strip_new_args` removes the literal `" --replication-host 127.0.0.1"`. The same value is the `replication_host` column of `deploy/backup-clusters.conf:21` and is already parsed into `ctx.main.replication_host` (`scripts/backup_clusters.py`, `BackupCluster.replication_host`), yet `step_apply` passes only `ctx.main.url_key` and `ctx.bucket_remote` into `production_changes`. AGENTS.md is explicit here: "Never scatter comparison values across code. If a value is used in conditionals, switch cases, or lookups, define it once … and reference that definition everywhere." Because this is the comparison that protects production's schedule (TD3), a table edit to `replication_host` would silently stop the check from recognising the argument 227 adds, and the test that asserts the pre-227 equivalence would keep passing against its own hardcoded copy. Pass the row's host through from `ctx.main` instead.

findings.title: New provision tests assert on script source text rather than behaviour
findings.description: `_script_assignments` greps the provisioning script for literal assignment lines and the tests compare exact strings, e.g. `test_only_trading_tick_is_created` asserts `_script_assignments("CREATED_DATABASES") == "CREATED_DATABASES=(trading_tick)"` and `test_roles_are_applied_with_replication` asserts `'-v with_replication=1 -f - < "$ROLES_SQL"' in body`. These break on harmless reformatting and cannot catch the regressions they name (a `with_replication` flag passed but the `\if` block deleted from the SQL would still satisfy the grep). The testing rules ask for behaviour over implementation (`_rendered_hba()`, which extracts and *runs* `hba_content` with a stubbed `client_source`, is the right shape and shows the pattern is available here). There is a project precedent for constant-definition greps (`test_interval_constant_defined_once`), so this is informational rather than blocking.

findings.title: Generated cutover report's `slice:` frontmatter does not follow the notes convention
findings.description: `render_report` emits `slice: backup-coverage-for-tick-archive-and-database`, whereas the sibling note it will sit beside, `project-documents/user/notes/2026-10-04-226-proof-drop-proof.md`, carries `slice: 226-slice.proof-on-existing-data` and also a `status:` field. AGENTS.md requires markdown frontmatter per `file-naming-conventions`, and the slice index/`-slice.` form is the one the existing note uses. The filename itself (`<date>-227-cutover.md`) is correct; only the metadata value and the missing `status` drift.

findings.title: Production's cron lines are reproduced exactly, with only the new argument pairs added
findings.description: Verified by reading the three inputs and tracing the logic rather than trusting the tests. `deploy/cron.d/manta-trading-backup` renders production's four jobs from `manta-trading-backup.cluster` with `@REPLICATION_HOST_ARG@` expanding to ` --replication-host 127.0.0.1` for `17/main` and to empty for `17/tick` (the table's `-`), and `_JOB_LINE`'s five-token prefix plus user field correctly separates `manta` jobs from the two `root` restic lines while ignoring `SHELL=`/`PATH=`/`MAILTO=` header lines. `production_lines` returns the `17/main` block followed by the host block, which matches the pre-227 file's order in `test/unit/fixtures/cron_main_pre227.txt`, so `production_changes`' `zip(..., strict=True)` comparison is a like-for-like line comparison. The `-` (bucket root) handling in `render_cron.sh` reproduces production's `--remote b2:<bucket>` unchanged, and the quoted `rep` in every `${x//pat/rep}` is what keeps `2>&1` from being rewritten under bash 5.2's `patsub_replacement`.
